import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

Reading the lead's report is done; now I'm reading the diagram manifest before restructuring.

Now I'll splice the manifest's mermaid fences in byte-for-byte, each with its italic caption inside a figure-anchor div.

Validating the result: checking fence identity, anchors, and that every line of the lead's text survived.

Every missing piece is a heading or bold run-in I deliberately restructured; all body text survived. Next I'm checking anchors with pandoc.

All checks pass: 3 fences, byte-identical; 3 figure divs; every in-document link resolves; the opening order is correct. Now I'll write the file (no overwrite) and register it.

The file is written and registered. Finishing with the final declaration.

I published the bank hub demotion report as `202611/bank_hub_demotion/bank_hub_demotion.md` and registered it as `research:202611/bank_hub_demotion/bank_hub_demotion.md` (ref `file:explicit:7baf7626d2fb564483b14115`). The host commits it to the research repo after this turn ends.

**Structure:** The file opens with the title, then a three-sentence research query, then the infographic (`bank_hub_demotion_infographic.png`, confirmed present beside the report), then `## Bottom line`, which is the lead's verdict and one-sentence target state. The rest follows the order a reader would ask in: ground truth, lead verification, the type decision, the migration trap, requirement adjustments A–H, recommended solution, risks, open questions, and scope and sources. The lead's opening scope paragraph and its "Where the detail lives" section are now in that last section.

- Headings are unnumbered and there is no table of contents.
- I took punctuation out of headings so their anchors work in both GitHub and the PDF, moving the dropped parts to each section's first line, e.g. "Untyped, by 4–1, and the lead agrees."
- Under "Recommended solution", the bold run-ins "Why the vault phase can land first", "Version skew to design for" and "Epic-level acceptance" became `###` subsections. I also added a "Phase plan" subsection heading over the phase table.
- I split one paragraph in "The migration trap" so the album-parent figure sits right after its anchor sentence, above the "Untyped bank.md without reparenting" list. No wording changed.

**Diagrams:** the manifest's status was `ready`, its `source` matches the lead's label, and all three anchors each matched exactly one block. All three are placed and none were omitted:

| Diagram | Anchor | Where it sits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type-edit-residue` | `#figure-type-edit-residue` | after the ground-truth list |
| `capture-picker-bypass` | `#figure-capture-picker-bypass` | after the lead-verification list |
| `album-parent-failure` | `#figure-album-parent-failure` | at the end of the anchor paragraph in "The migration trap" |

**Checks:**
- **Diagrams:** each manifest mermaid block appears exactly once and byte-identical. The lead's report had no mermaid diagrams, so the published file has 3. There are 3 figure divs, and pandoc shows all three figure IDs.
- **Links:** every in-document link (`#...`) points to a heading or figure ID that exists. The lead's report had no external URLs, relative links or repository-file links, so nothing needed fixing and nothing was unrepairable.
- **Text and table:** a sentence-by-sentence comparison found all of the lead's body text present. The only differences are the reworded headings and run-ins. Every cell of the five-phase table carried over.

**Problems along the way:** `sase artifact read` would not open the diagram manifest by its `research:` label (that path type is filtered out), so I read it through its `file:explicit:` ref instead. There was no `research.6h.image` variable to read with `sase var get`, so I used the `diagrams` variable as given in the prompt (`status: ready`). Neither problem affected the published file.
